en.title: Makhana Kheer
en.description: A creamy, delicious pudding made from Fox Nuts (Makhana), a staple of Mithila.
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and roast the Makhana on low heat until they become crisp.
Crush 1/3rd of the roasted Makhana coarsely. Keep the rest whole.
Boil the milk in a heavy-bottomed pot. Reduce the flame and let it thicken slightly.
Add the roasted Makhana (both whole and crushed) to the boiling milk.
Cook on low heat for 10-15 minutes until the Makhana softens and the milk thickens.
Add sugar, cardamom powder, and nuts. Cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Serve warm or chilled.
en.culturalSignificance: Makhana is considered auspicious in Mithila and is often served during weddings and festivals. This kheer is a healthier alternative to rice kheer.

hi.title: मखानक खीर
hi.description: मखाना की खीर एक स्वादिष्ट और पौष्टिक मिठाई है, जो मिथिला में बहुत लोकप्रिय है।
instructions: एक कड़ाही में घी गर्म करें और मखाने को कुरकुरा होने तक भूनें।
भुने हुए मखाने का एक तिहाई हिस्सा दरदरा पीस लें। बाकी को साबुत रखें।
एक भारी तले वाले बर्तन में दूध उबालें। आंच कम करें और इसे थोड़ा गाढ़ा होने दें।
उबलते दूध में भुने हुए मखाने (साबुत और पिसे हुए) डालें।
धीमी आंच पर 10-15 मिनट तक पकाएं जब तक मखाना नरम न हो जाए और दूध गाढ़ा न हो जाए।
चीनी, इलायची पाउडर और मेवे डालें। 2-3 मिनट और पकाएं।
आंच बंद कर दें। गर्मागर्म या ठंडा करके परोसें।
hi.culturalSignificance: मिथिला में मखाना को शुभ माना जाता है और इसे अक्सर शादियों और त्योहारों के दौरान परोसा जाता है।

mai.title: मखानक खीर
mai.description: मखानक खीर मिथिलाक एकटा प्रमुख आर स्वादिष्ट मिठाई थिक।
instructions: कड़ाही में घी गर्म करू आर मखान के कुरकुरा होय तक भुजू।
भुजल मखान के एक तिहाई हिस्सा दरदरा क क कूटि लिय। बाकी के साबुत राखू।
एकटा भारी पेंदी वाला बर्तन में दूध खौलाउ। आंच कम क क एकरा तनी गाढ़ होय दिय।
खौलैत दूध में भुजल मखान (साबुत आर कुटल) द दिय।
कम आंच पर १०-१५ मिनट तक पकाउ जब तक मखान नरम नहि भ जाय आर दूध गाढ़ नहि भ जाय।
चीनी, इलायची पाउडर आर मेवा दिय। २-३ मिनट आर पकाउ।
आंच बंद क दिय। गरम या ठंडा क क परसू।
mai.culturalSignificance: मिथिला में मखान के शुभ मानल जायत छैक आर ई विवाह-डांगा आर पावनि-तिहार में अक्सर बनाओल जायत छैक।

en.title: Thekua
en.description: A traditional crispy sweet cookie made of whole wheat flour and jaggery, essential for Chhath Puja.
ingredients: 1 cup Jaggery (melted in 1/2 cup water) or Sugar
Oil or Ghee for deep frying
instructions: In a large bowl, mix wheat flour, ghee, cardamom powder, fennel seeds, and coconut.
Rub the ghee into the flour using your fingers until it resembles breadcrumbs (Moyan).
Add the cooled jaggery syrup (or sugar water) little by little to knead a stiff dough.
Pinch small balls of dough and press them against a Thekua mould (archa) to create patterns.
Heat oil/ghee in a kadhai on medium flame.
Deep fry the Thekuas on low-medium heat until golden brown and crispy.
en.culturalSignificance: Thekua is the main "Prasad" offering to the Sun God during the Chhath Puja festival. It is known for its long shelf life.

hi.title: ठेकुआ
hi.description: ठेकुआ छठ पूजा का मुख्य प्रसाद है। यह गेहूं के आटे और गुड़ से बना एक पारंपरिक कुरकुरा मीठा व्यंजन है।
ingredients: तलने के लिए तेल या घी
instructions: एक बड़े बर्तन में आटा, घी, इलायची पाउडर, सौंफ और नारियल मिलाएं।
घी को आटे में अच्छी तरह मिलाएं (मोयन)।
गुड़ का पानी थोड़ा-थोड़ा डालकर सख्त आटा गूंथ लें।
आटे की छोटी लोइयां बनाएं और उन्हें ठेकुआ के सांचे (अरचा) पर दबाकर आकार दें।
धीमी आंच पर तेल/घी गर्म करें और सुनहरा होने तक तलें।
ठंडा होने पर एयरटाइट डिब्बे में रखें।
hi.culturalSignificance: ठेकुआ छठ पूजा के दौरान सूर्य देव को चढ़ाया जाने वाला मुख्य प्रसाद है। यह लंबे समय तक खराब नहीं होता है।

mai.title: ठेकुआ
mai.description: ठेकुआ छठ पूजाक मुख्य प्रसाद थिक। ई गहूम क आटा आर गुड़ स बनल एकटा पारंपरिक पकवान थिक।
instructions: एकटा पैघ बर्तन में आटा, घी, इलायची, सौंफ आर गड़ी मिलाउ।
घी के आटा में नीक जकां मिलाउ (मोयन)।
गुड़ क पानी तनी-तनी द क कड़ा सानू।
आटा क छोट-छोट लोई बनाउ आर ओकरा ठेकुआ क अरचा पर दबा क आकार दिय।
कम आंच पर तेल/घी गर्म करू आर लाल होय तक छानू।
ठंडा भेला पर डब्बा में राखू।
mai.culturalSignificance: ठेकुआ छठ पावनि में सूर्य देवता के चढ़ाओल जाय वाला मुख्य प्रसाद थिक।

en.title: Tilkor Tarua (Fritters)
en.description: Crispy fritters made from leaves of the Pointed Gourd (Parwal/Patal) creeper.
instructions: Wash the Tilkor leaves gently and pat them dry.
Make a thick batter using rice flour, besan, spices, salt, and water.
Heat mustard oil in a pan.
Dip each leaf into the batter, ensuring it is well coated.
Deep fry or shallow fry until crispy and golden.
Serve hot with meals as a side dish.
en.culturalSignificance: Tilkor is unique to the Mithila region. Serving Tilkor Tarua to guests is considered a mark of respect and hospitality.

en.title: Dahi Chura
en.description: A wholesome breakfast staple consisting of beaten rice (Chura/Poha) and yogurt, typically eaten with sugar or jaggery.
instructions: Wash the Chura lightly if it is thick, or use it dry if it is crisp.
Pour thick fresh curd over it.
en.culturalSignificance: It is the mandatory breakfast on the day of Makar Sankranti (Til Sakraat) in Mithila. It is famously known as "comfort food" for Maithils.

en.title: Mithila Fish Curry
en.description: Spicy fish curry cooked in a pungent mustard paste gravy, a signature dish of the region.
instructions: Marinate fish pieces with salt and turmeric.
Fry the fish in hot mustard oil until golden. Set aside.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds for tempering.
Add the mustard and garlic paste. Sauté well.
Add spices and tomatoes. Cook until oil separates.
Add water to make the gravy.
Once gravy boils, add the fried fish pieces.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Garnish with coriander.
en.culturalSignificance: Fish is a symbol of fertility and auspiciousness in Mithila ("Maachh-Bhaat"). No celebration is complete without it for non-vegetarians.

en.title: Ol (Yam) Chutney
en.description: A tangy and spicy chutney made from Elephant Foot Yam (Ol), known for its distinct flavor.
instructions: Add raw mustard oil, mustard powder, green chilies, and salt.
Add lemon juice generously (to reduce the itchiness of the yam).
Mix well. Can be stored for a few days.
en.culturalSignificance: Ol is traditionally eaten on Diwali to ensure prosperity. It keeps the body warm during winter.

en.title: Dal Pithi
en.description: Flower-shaped wheat dumplings cooked in spicy lentil soup. A hearty one-pot meal.
instructions: Pressure cook the dal with turmeric and salt until half done.
Roll out the wheat dough and cut into small flower shapes (Pithi).
Add the Pithis to the boiling dal.
Simmer until the dumplings are cooked through.
Temper with ghee, cumin, and red chilies.
en.culturalSignificance: A simple, nutritious comfort meal often made for dinner in Maithil households.

en.title: Bagiya
en.description: Steamed rice flour dumplings stuffed with lentils or jaggery/khoya. A healthy, oil-free snack.
ingredients: Filling Option 1: Chana Dal paste with spices
Filling Option 2: Khoa/Mawa with sugar and nuts
instructions: Mix hot water with rice flour to make a soft dough.
Take a small ball, hollow it out, and fill with the chosen stuffing.
Seal it into an oval shape tapered at both ends.
Steam in a steamer for 15-20 minutes.
en.culturalSignificance: Traditionally eaten during the winter season, especially on the auspicious day of Pous Sankranti.

en.title: Adauri (Badi)
en.description: Sun-dried lentil dumplings used to enhance the flavor of vegetable curries.
instructions: Grind the soaked dal into a fine paste.
Beat the batter until fluffy (it should float in water).
Mix in spices and grated melon.
Drop small dumplings onto a cloth sheet in strong sunlight.
Dry for 3-4 days until hard. Store in jars.
en.culturalSignificance: Making Adauri is a community activity for women in summer. These are used throughout the year in curries with potatoes or eggplant.

en.title: Khaja
en.description: Layered crispy sweet pastry, famously from Silao but integral to Mithila weddings.
instructions: Knead a firm dough with flour, ghee, and water.
Stack 3-4 sheets with a smear of ghee and flour paste between them.
Roll the stack into a log and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Deep fry on low heat until layers open up and turn golden.
en.culturalSignificance: Khaja is a mandatory item in the "Sandesh" (gifts) sent to the daughter's in-laws.

en.title: Arikanchan (Colocasia Curry)
en.description: Spicy, tangy curry made from rolled Colocasia leaves (Arbi Patta) stuffed with gram flour paste.
instructions: Make a thick paste of besan, amchur, spices, and water.
Layer leaves one on top of another, spreading the paste between each layer.
Roll the stack tightly and steam for 15-20 minutes.
Cool, cut into slices, and shallow fry.
Prepare a mustard-based gravy and add the fried rolls (this is the "Sabba").
en.culturalSignificance: A delicacy in Mithila, often made when Arbi leaves are lush green during monsoons. It serves as a mock-meat dish.

en.title: Pidakiya (Gujiya)
en.description: A deep-fried dumpling stuffed with sweet khoya and nuts, crucial for Tij and Holi.
instructions: Knead a stiff dough with maida and ghee.
Roast khoya/suji until golden and mix with sugar, coconut, and nuts.
Roll out small circles of dough.
Place filling in the center, fold, and seal edges (often designing with a fork or hand).
Deep fry on low heat until golden brown.
en.culturalSignificance: Mandatory for the "Tij" festival. Women compete to make the most beautifully designed Pidakiya.

en.title: Anarasa
en.description: A sweet pastry made from soaked rice flour and jaggery, coated with sesame seeds.
instructions: Grind the semi-moist rice into a coarse powder.
Mix with sugar/jaggery. The mixture effectively becomes a dough due to the rice moisture.
Leave the dough for a few hours/days to ferment slightly (optional).
Make small flat discs, coat one side with sesame seeds.
Deep fry with the sesame side up until golden.
en.culturalSignificance: A delicacy made during Diwali and Holi.

hi.title: अनरसा
hi.description: चावल के आटे और गुड़ से बनी, तिल लगी हुई कुरकुरी पेस्ट्री।
instructions: भीगे चावल को पीसकर आटा बनाएं।
छोटी लोई बनाएं, तिल लगाएं और तलें।
hi.culturalSignificance: दिवाली और होली के दौरान बनाई जाने वाली एक मिठाई।

mai.title: अनरसा
mai.description: चाउर क आटा आर गुड़ स बनल मिठाई।
instructions: चाउर फूलने दिय आर पीस लिय।
mai.culturalSignificance: दीवाली आर होली क समय बनैत अछि।

en.title: Kadhi Bari
en.description: Soft gram flour dumplings (Bari) simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy (Kadhi).
ingredients: Dry Red Chilies and Curry Leaves for tempering
instructions: Mix besan, water, and spices to make a thick batter for Bari.
Deep fry small dumplings (Baris) in mustard oil until fluffy.
Mix curd, remaining besan, turmeric, and water to make a thin liquid.
Cook this liquid on low heat until it boils and thickens (Kadhi).
Add the fried Baris and simmer.
Temper with hing, red chilies, and curry leaves.
en.culturalSignificance: Kadhi-Bari is the celebratory Sunday lunch and a must-have for guests. The softness of the Bari is a test of the cook's skill (`Phulouri`).

en.title: Ghugni Mudhi
en.description: A spicy black gram or yellow pea curry served with puffed rice (Mudhi). The ultimate evening snack.
ingredients: 1 cup Black Gram (Kala Chana) or Yellow Peas (soaked)
instructions: Heat oil in a cooker or pan.
Add soaked chana and spices. Sauté high heat.
Add water and cook until chana is tender but keeps shape.
Serve hot in a bowl, topped with raw onions, alongside a heap of Mudhi.
en.culturalSignificance: The common man's breakfast and evening snack across Mithila and Bengal. Cheap, nutritious, and filling.

en.title: Kachri (Onion Fritters)
en.description: Rustic onion fritters bound with gram flour or crushed pulses, fried to perfection.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Besan or Soaked Masoor Dal paste
instructions: Mix sliced onions with salt and leave for 5 mins to release water.
Add spices and binding agent (besan/dal paste). Do not add water.
Heat oil. Drop irregular lumps of the mixture into hot oil.
Serve with puffed rice (Mudhi) or chutney.
en.culturalSignificance: A favorite rainy day snack. Often pairs with Mudhi (`Mudhi-Kachri`).

en.title: Tisi (Flaxseed) Chutney
en.description: A dry, nutty chutney made from roasted flaxseeds, garlic, and chilies.
instructions: Dry roast the flaxseeds and red chilies until they pop.
Grind into a fine powder along with garlic and salt.
Before serving, mix a small amount with a few drops of water and raw mustard oil.
en.culturalSignificance: Tisi is a winter superfood in Mithila, known to keep the body warm. This chutney is a staple side for rice and daal.

en.title: Dhaniya Chutney (Silbatta Style)
en.description: Fresh coriander chutney ground on a stone slab (Silbatta) for maximum flavor preservation.
instructions: Roast the tomato on an open flame until skin chars. Peel it.
Place coriander, chilies, garlic, and roasted tomato in a grinder (or Silbatta).
Mix in salt and a dash of raw mustard oil.
en.culturalSignificance: Essential winter condiment found in every Maithil lunch plate.

en.title: Malpua
en.description: Soft, fluffy pancakes soaked in sugar syrup, often containing bananas.
instructions: Mash bananas and mix with flour, milk, and fennel seeds to make a pouring consistency batter.
Heat ghee in a flat pan.
Pour a ladleful of batter. Do not spread it; let it take its shape.
Fry until golden brown edges appear.
Soak in warm sugar syrup for 2 mins and serve.
en.culturalSignificance: The star dessert of Holi celebrations in Mithila.

en.title: Nenua Chana Dal
en.description: Sponge gourd (Toro) cooked with soaked gram lentils—a healthy, nutritious vegetable dish.
instructions: Add soaked chana dal and spices.
Add the sliced Nenua. (Nenua releases a lot of water, so no extra water needed usually).
Cover and cook until dal is soft and veggies are tender.
en.culturalSignificance: A very common summer vegetable dish, valued for being cooling and easy to digest.

en.title: Baigan Adauri
en.description: Eggplant curry enhanced with the strong flavor of sun-dried lentil dumplings (Adauri).
instructions: Fry the Adauri in oil until red/brown. Remove.
In the same oil, add spices/mustard paste.
Add water and the fried Adauri.
Cook until veggies and Adauri are soft. The Adauri absorbs the gravy.
en.culturalSignificance: A classic way to use preserved Adauri during seasons when fresh vegetables might be scarce.

en.title: Sattu Sharbat
en.description: The energy drink of Bihar/Mithila. Roasted gram flour powder mixed with water and spices.
ingredients: Finely of chopped Onion & Green Chili (optional)
instructions: Add 1/2 water and stir to remove lumps.
Add salt, spices, onion, and lemon juice.
en.culturalSignificance: The ultimate coolant for the scorching summers. Farmers drink this for instant energy (`Sattu-Pani`).

en.title: Kathal (Jackfruit) Curry
en.description: Raw jackfruit curry that rivals mutton in texture and taste.
instructions: Fry the jackfruit cubes until golden. Set aside.
In oil, add whole spices and onion paste. Brown it well.
Add ginger-garlic and powdered spices. Cook until oil separates.
Pressure cook for 1-2 whistles until soft.
en.culturalSignificance: Often called "Vegetarian Mutton" (`Ahuna Kathal`), served on special occasions like Holi.

en.title: Ol (Yam) Curry
en.description: A rich, spicy curry made from Elephant Foot Yam, often resembling meat curry.
ingredients: Amchur or Lemon (crucial to prevent itching)
instructions: Deep fry the boiled Yam cubes.
Prepare a gravy using mustard paste, garlic, and spices.
en.culturalSignificance: Mandatory dish on Diwali. It signifies strength and longevity.

en.title: Laai (Puffed Rice Balls)
en.description: Crispy balls made of puffed rice (Mudhi) or beaten rice (Chura) bound with sticky jaggery syrup.
ingredients: 3 cups Puffed Rice (Mudhi) or Roasted Chura
instructions: Melt jaggery with a little water to hard-ball consistency.
Turn off heat and quickly mix in the puffed rice.
Grease hands with water/ghee and shape the hot mixture into balls.
en.culturalSignificance: A common winter treat, especially during Makar Sankranti.

en.title: Red Amaranth Greens
en.description: Simple, nutritious stir-fry of red leafy greens, a common lunch item.
instructions: Wash and chop the saag finely.
Heat mustard oil, add garlic and red chilies.
Cover and cook on low heat until water evaporates.
en.culturalSignificance: Rich in iron, this saag is a poor man's superfood in Mithila.

hi.title: लाल साग
hi.description: लाल साग एक सरल और पौष्टिक डिश है, जो दोपहर के भोजन में आम है।
instructions: साग को धोकर बारीक काट लें।
तेल गर्म करें, लहसुन और मिर्च डालें।
hi.culturalSignificance: आयरन से भरपूर, यह मिथिला में गरीबों का सुपरफूड माना जाता है।

mai.title: लाल साग
mai.description: लाल साग एकटा साधारण मुदा पौष्टिक तरकारी थिक, जे अक्सर दुपहरिया लंच में बनाओल जायत अछि।
instructions: साग के धो क महीन काटू।
तेल गरम क क लहसुन-मिर्च दिय।
साग और नून द क तोप दिय।
mai.culturalSignificance: लाल साग खून बढ़ाबै लेल बहुत नीक मानल जायत छैक।

en.title: Bathua Greens
en.description: Winter special greens, often cooked with potatoes or plain.
instructions: Boil bathua and mash it (for Jhor) or stir fry with potatoes (Bhujia).
For Bhujia: Heat oil, add cumin/chilies.
Add potatoes, fry till half done.
Add chopped Bathua and cook till dry.
en.culturalSignificance: Available only in winter, it is known for keeping the body warm.

hi.title: बथुआ (बथुआ साग)
hi.description: सर्दियों का विशेष साग, जिसे अक्सर आलू के साथ या सादा बनाया जाता है।
instructions: बथुआ को उबालकर मैश करें (झोर के लिए) या आलू के साथ भूनें (भुजिया)।
भुजिया के लिए: तेल गर्म करें, जीरा/मिर्च डालें।
आलू डालें, आधा पकने तक भूनें।
कटा हुआ बथुआ डालें और सूखने तक पकाएं।
hi.culturalSignificance: केवल सर्दियों में उपलब्ध, यह शरीर को गर्म रखने के लिए जाना जाता है।

mai.title: बथुआ (बथुआ साग)
mai.description: जाड़ क स्पेशल साग, जेकरा आलू क संग या ऐसे ही बनाओल जायत अछि।
instructions: बथुआ के उसइन क महीन क लिय (झोर लेल) या आलू संग भुजू (भुजिया)।
भुजिया लेल: तेल गरम क जीरा/मिर्च दिय।
बथुआ द क पानी सुखला तक भुजू।
mai.culturalSignificance: ई साग खाली जाड़ में भेटैत अछि आर शरीर के गरम रखैत अछि।

en.title: Spinach Curry (Mithila Style)
en.description: Spinach cooked with eggplant and radish, flavored with mustard oil.
instructions: Add eggplant and radish, fry slightly.
Drizzle raw mustard oil on top before serving.
en.culturalSignificance: The addition of raw mustard oil (Kachchi Ghani) is the signature of Maithil cooking.

hi.title: पालक साग (मिथिला स्टाइल)
hi.description: बैंगन और मूली के साथ पकाया गया पालक, सरसों के तेल के स्वाद के साथ।
instructions: तेल गर्म करें, पंच फोरन डालें।
